long_description:
This three-day intensive is for yoga teachers (with any level of certification) who want to learn how to teach pregnant people safely and confidently.
This course offers foundational preparation and a practical base for teaching hapū students in all stages of pregnancy in public yoga classes.
What's covered:
*Hormonal and structural changes across each trimester
*Pelvic floor anatomy and its relevance to yoga practice
*Birth-supportive movement and positioning
*Common pregnancy ailments and how to adapt your teaching
*Contraindications and safety considerations
*Inclusive, trauma-aware cueing for pregnant students

Facilitator:
Marcelly Ribeiro (she/her; they/them) is a Brazilian-born yoga teacher and dancer based in Aotearoa New Zealand for the past 10 years. She holds a degree in Physical Education, 200-hour Vinyasa and Hatha Yoga Teacher Trainings, and certifications in Childbirth Education, Doula support, and Active Birth. Her teaching blends alignment-based yoga with the fluidity and expression of dance, reflecting her belief that both practices are powerful tools for connection, presence, and self-awareness. Specialising in prenatal yoga, Marcelly integrates asana, pranayama, and birth education to support women in preparing their bodies and minds for labour.

long_description:
The Inner Journey: Story-Led Sound Bath
Across cultures and throughout history, stories have guided people inward, offering wisdom, comfort, and connection. This immersive sound bath blends ancient poetic narratives with the soothing sounds of harmonium, flutes, crystal bowls, and gentle voice to create a space of stillness, reflection, and deep listening.
Mats, blankets and cushions are provided but feel free to bring anything else to aid your comfort.
Meet Smita, your host:
From a young age, Smita was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.
Meet Alexandra, your host:
Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

name: CREATION
venue: 111 Wakefield St, Wellington
long_description:
Orchestra Wellington takes the stage with Ballet Collective Aotearoa to present Darius Milhaud’s "La Création du Monde", a work, described as “a milestone in cross-Atlantic pollination”. Inspired by his visits to Harlem and to New York bars and clubs, Milhaud weds European art music to jazz harmonies and melodies. “Against the beat of the drums, the melodic lines criss-crossed in a breathless patter of broken and twisted rhythms.”
Bartók’s concerto adapts his Sonata for Two Pianos and Percussion to bring more sonorities to this striking blend of Expressionism and Hungarian folk music. Orchestra Wellington is joined by the John Psathas Group, fittingly named for our Patron, John Psathas, whose percussion compositions are also internationally sought-after.
Nielsen’s Symphony No. 4 is fully invested in the composer’s unique voice, which is wild and wayward as a storm outdoors, mysterious as a forest glade in the northern pine woods. Amid so much death, Nielsen contended that music was life: “As soon as even a single note sounds in the air or through space, it is the result of life and movement; that is why music (and dance) are the more immediate expressions of the will to live. The symphony evokes the most primal sources of life and the wellspring of the life-feeling; that is, what lies behind all human, animal and plant life, as we perceive or live it. Life is indomitable and inextinguishable…”

long_description:
This three-day intensive is for yoga teachers (with any level of certification) who want to learn how to teach pregnant people safely and confidently.
This course offers foundational preparation and a practical base for teaching hapū students in all stages of pregnancy in public yoga classes.
What's covered:
*Hormonal and structural changes across each trimester
*Pelvic floor anatomy and its relevance to yoga practice
*Birth-supportive movement and positioning
*Common pregnancy ailments and how to adapt your teaching
*Contraindications and safety considerations
*Inclusive, trauma-aware cueing for pregnant students

Facilitator:
Marcelly Ribeiro (she/her; they/them) is a Brazilian-born yoga teacher and dancer based in Aotearoa New Zealand for the past 10 years. She holds a degree in Physical Education, 200-hour Vinyasa and Hatha Yoga Teacher Trainings, and certifications in Childbirth Education, Doula support, and Active Birth. Her teaching blends alignment-based yoga with the fluidity and expression of dance, reflecting her belief that both practices are powerful tools for connection, presence, and self-awareness. Now - more than ever - there is a focus on self-care and a revitalisation of our traditional healing practices.

www.pierrebonvalot.com/good-questions

• Leave a message in the comment section to let the others know that you will actually be there (I don’t want you to end up alone there

• If you can’t make it anymore, no problem! But please update your RSVP to let the others know
• Please be gentle and patient with each other. We all want to make good friends here.

venue: 10 Whitcher Grove, Wainuiomata
long_description:
We’ve teamed up with the Wellington Astronomical Society to bring you this exclusive FREE behind-the-scenes event.
Walk deep into untouched native forest, through some of the oldest trees in the Wellington region as darkness falls. You may even hear the calls of kiwi and rūrū (morepork). Explore an area not normally open to the public, including a glowworm-filled tunnel that links to the Orongorongo Valley.
The Wellington Astronomical Society will share insights on Dark Sky awareness and preservation and provide a telescope for viewing the Moon and the Southern Cross. Talk to Remutaka Conservation Trust volunteers about their Kiwi release programme and nest monitoring efforts.
Wainuiomata Regional Park is working towards dark sky reserve accreditation, one of only three in the Southern Hemisphere. Light pollution from the city washes out most stars, but the park offers one of the best stargazing experiences in the region.
What to bring:
• Torches/headlamps (red lenses preferred)
• Sturdy waterproof footwear
• Warm and wet weather clothing
Note: This event includes a steep hill walk in the dark. A moderate level of fitness is required, and it is not suitable for children under 15.
This event is strictly limited to 30 people. Registrations for this event will be on a first in first served basis and opens at 10am on Tuesday 14 July via this link: https://forms.office.com/r/Q1pZh7yG4F

id: Stained Glass - 4 Week Block - Fridays!-3 Market Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Facebook
name: Stained Glass - 4 Week Block - Fridays!
venue: 3 Market Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Spend four inspiring evenings immersed in the beautiful art of stained glass and leadlighting at our welcoming waterfront studio in Market Lane. Whether you are completely new to glasswork or already have some experience, this relaxed and supportive 4-week class is a wonderful opportunity to slow down, get creative, and make something truly special by hand.
The course starts on Friday 21 August and runs for 4 weeks till Friday 11 September, 5.30pm - 8.30pm.
Guided by our experienced tutors, you will learn the traditional techniques used to create stunning leadlight and stained glass pieces, while developing the confidence to design and complete your own projects. Beginners will start with a simple and elegant clear glass project, learning each stage of the process step-by-step — from planning a design and safely cutting glass, to grinding, foiling, soldering, and finishing your piece.
Once you have mastered the basics, you will have the freedom to move on to colourful sun-catchers, decorative panels, small hanging pieces, or more detailed designs depending on your interests and experience level. Students with prior experience are encouraged to work on more complex projects with guidance from the tutor.
This is a warm, friendly, and highly supportive class where students can work at their own pace while enjoying the inspiring atmosphere of our creative studio community. It is the perfect Friday night creative escape — a chance to unwind, learn new skills, and create beautiful handmade glass pieces you will treasure for years to come.
All tools and equipment are supplied, and you are very welcome to bring along your own glass or tools if you already have them.
Glass, copper foil, solder, and other consumable materials are additional and can be purchased from the studio as needed for your projects.
Beginners can expect to pay around $50 - $80 in materials depending on their projects.
Course fee $315, Early bird $284 till 27 July.

Ever wondered how to strut your stuff in heels with confidence and flair?
The secret lies in mastering the technique! From flawless walks and captivating combos to strength-building exercises and perfect posture, it’s all about technique and practice. By the end of the five weeks, you can expect to feel more grounded, technically aware, and confident in their ability to move with clarity, control, and presence in heels.
Why is heel technique important?
- Safety First: Proper technique prevents injuries, ensuring you can dance for years to come.
- Strength & Posture: Build the muscles needed to support your ankles, knees, and back, while perfecting that elegant posture.
- Confidence Boost: Knowing you have the technique down pat gives you the confidence to own the floor!
Whether you’re a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class will cover:
- Walks that turn heads
- Seamless combos
- Targeted exercises for strength
- Posture tips to keep you looking and feeling your best
To receive the full benefit of the course, we encourage commitment to all five consecutive Saturday's, beginning 18th July.
Spaces are intentionally limited to create a supportive, focused learning space and to allow for individual development throughout the course.

Meet at the Founders’ entrance to Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā on Glenmore Street. Please bring your ticket, a torch, and an umbrella if it’s raining. We'll see you there!
This tour is operated by the Friends of Wellington Botanic Garden.
